translation:
Sadguru Jivanji says: "Kabir is the form of the Primal Being [Adi Purush]. He showed grace upon Gnaniji, and Gnaniji understood Kabirji to be none other than Ram himself. He did not regard the Sadguru and God as separate. He united Sadguru Kabir and Ram as one, and established the term Ramkabir."

Gnaniji's manifestation [birth] was in Samvat 1451, Posh Sud 11. Gnaniji's living samadhi [conscious departure from the body] took place in Samvat 1559, Posh Sud 11. In Mota Sanja there is a Tulsi platform marking Gnaniji's samadhi. The neem tree under which Gnaniji used to sit was once split into two by a lightning strike, but it sprouted again and has grown fresh leaves once more; the leaves of this neem carry no bitterness. Mota Sanja can be reached from Zaghadia. Kabirji came to Gujarat from Kashi, and visited Patan Padmavadi, the courtyard of Narsinh Mehta in Junagadh, Pipaji's place in Gangrod fort, and Tattvajiva's place in Mangaleshwar (at Kabirvad).

Haridas Nadiada and Vaishnav Shyamdasji Maharaj, who have narrated the life-story and philosophical teachings of Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj, have made no mention at all of certain episodes of his life. Either Jivanji Maharaj himself did not inform anyone of certain events in his life, or he simply paid no attention to recording them. One such matter is that of his birth, his birthplace, and information about his parents — regarding this, we have not been able to obtain any definite information.

Vaishnav Haridas Nadiada, the earliest editor of the Samagam [the collection of teachings], writes about Jivanji Maharaj's manifestation that he appeared at Gahej Goriyad on Shravan Sud Eighth of Samvat 1660, at the age of eleven. But interpreting this sentence in light of his couplets [sakhis] and the references found within the Samagam, it appears that on this day he renounced his home and adopted the life of a mendicant. Since he had already crossed eleven years of age in Samvat 1660, his birth must have taken place in Samvat 1649. Furthermore, the genealogist's records state that he was originally born into a Leva Patidar family of Karamsad, and that he lost the shelter of his parents in his childhood. It was therefore in this condition that he renounced his home and took initiation at Gahej Goriyad. However, this record makes no mention at all of the names of his parents.

Whatever the truth may be, he must certainly have been born somewhere, and for some reason he must have renounced his home and begun his wanderings. And at the age of thirty-four, in Samvat 1683, he bowed to Gopaldas, addressing him as Ramkabir, and accepted him as his Sadguru. Thus, on this day, he accepted the Ramkabir tradition. But where he stayed and what he did during all these intervening years, he himself never mentioned to anyone, nor have Haridas Nadiada or Shyamdasji made any mention of it.
